Check against the spec at https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28 (transports/stdio, transports/streamable-http, server/discover, subscriptions) using WebFetch. Hunt for REAL defects, rank by severity (MAJOR = wrong behavior, security issue, hang, leak, regression for existing legacy servers; MINOR; NIT). Specifically challenge:
1. Regression risk for non-opted-in servers and for legacy servers (probe only when notify_cfg is Some; is that really airtight? what if request() of a legacy server now changes? the request/request_raw split must keep error handling identical).
2. Era detection per spec: is falling back correct on every non-modern outcome incl. timeout (8s) and HTTP 400/404/405 WITH a recognized modern error body (spec says do NOT fall back then; the code treats anything non-DiscoverResult-with-2026 as legacy; is that a defect for -32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersion or HeaderMismatch? what happens after the discover timeout leaves a late response/pending entry?). After fallback on HTTP, is protocol_version header state clean (set to Some(modern) before the probe)? Could a failed probe poison the legacy initialize?
3. stdio ListenRoute: shared stdout correlation, id collisions with request_id counter (listen id comes from the same AtomicU64), overflow behavior, race between install() and ack, close on reader EOF, notifications/cancelled handling, a response with the listen id but also stray method. Does pending map get a stray response for the listen id (leak)? What if the server answers the listen request with an error?
4. HTTP HttpListen: auth refresh path, 401 handling, size/bounds (no total cap on long streams, per-event bounds via SseParser), keepalive comments, drop = cancel (is the response dropped when the stream is dropped?), Mcp-Name base64 encoding correctness vs spec Value Encoding rules (sentinel, leading/trailing space, non-ASCII, empty), headers also required on notifications? Are Mcp-Method headers sent for legacy-era POSTs by mistake?
5. supervisor (listen.rs::supervise): reconnect/backoff/give-up policy, cancellation during backoff and during run_listen, `closed()` check, behavior when the engine's session state (acked/active classes) is reset by begin_listen on reconnect, reconcile after reconnect, and whether an immediate graceful end after a HONORED ack loops too fast (short_runs counting) or too slow. Does listen_honored() reflect the LATEST stream?
6. Trust: notifications remain hints only; opt-in only from global config (unchanged); resource/prompt tool output is untrusted data: injection via server name/uri/content, delimiter escaping, size bounds, policy parity with `mcp action=call`, reconnect behavior without replaying calls.
7. Test quality: do tests fail for the right reason (a mutation was done by the coordinator on empty-ack rule and stdio routing; suggest more), any flaky timing (sleep-based, 2.5s wait), anything claimed but untested. Also check tasks.md claims once the coordinator updates them (re-read it at the end).
Also list anything the spec requires that is not implemented, and anything implemented that the spec forbids (e.g. sending resources/subscribe in modern era, sending initialize to a modern server, sending notifications/initialized).
